newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian dollar holds steady despite US sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Australian dollar holds steady despite US sell-off.

text.p: The Australian dollar continued to show resilience on Monday against the heavy fall in U.S. financial markets on Friday.

Traders expressed surprised that the local dollar had managed to hold onto last week's gains, particularly amid concerns that local asset markets might continue to sell off if Wall St extended its decline.
"People are a little wary of selling the Aussie given how it's performed technically," a trader at Bankers Trust said.

In early trading, the Australian stock exchange fell by 76.4 points or 2.9 percent to a low of 2589.8, but recovered some ground by the close. The All Ordinaries Index closed at 2618.5, down 1.79 percent from Friday's close.
The Nikkei 225 Index also fell by more than two percent in early trade, before recovering some ground. By 5.00 p.m. (0700) the Nikkei stood at 19041.10, down 1.47 percent from Friday's close.
Treasury Secretary Ted Evans appeared before a parliamentary committee this morning, and gave an upbeat on the outlook for the economy.
